obs: “who can believe that they intended in the ninth section of that very act to use language which ought to be construed so as to deprive them entirely of a jury trial”

"Maintenance of the jury as a fact-finding body is of such importance and occupies so firm a place in our history and jurisprudence that any seeming curtailment of the right to a jury trial should be scrutinized with the utmost care."

"Even in construing statutes and rules governing civil cases we have taken pains, as Congress commanded, to resolve all doubts in favor of trial by jury . . . . We should certainly be equally alert to construe statutes governing trials for criminal contempt so as to protect the right of jury trial"
"The historic rule at the time was that, absent contrary provision by rule or statute, jury trial was not required in the case of either civil or criminal contempt."
